title: Classic Cheeseburger
subtitle: Beef patty with American cheese, lettuce, tomato, and pickles
excerpt: A classic cheeseburger is a beef patty, seasoned with salt and pepper only, cooked until it has a dark crust, topped with a slice of melted American-style cheese, and served in a soft bun with lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles. The quality of the beef and the quality of the bun determine the quality of the burger.
sourceNotes: The American cheeseburger developed in the 1920s and 1930s as a variation on the hamburger. The addition of a slice of cheese became standard by the mid-20th century. The American diner cheeseburger is the default version in the UK and throughout the world.

recipe.batchNotes: Form and refrigerate patties up to 24 hours ahead.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Patties can be formed and refrigerated overnight, but cook from cold.
recipe.temperatureNote: cast-iron or griddle pan over very high heat

content.text: A good cheeseburger depends on the beef and the crust. Use beef mince with at least 20% fat: lean mince produces a dry, compact patty. Season generously with salt and pepper and shape loosely: a tightly packed patty is dense and tough. Cook in a very hot pan without moving until a dark crust forms on the underside before flipping once.

Divide the beef into 4 equal portions (about 150 g each). Shape loosely into patties about 1.5 cm thick and 1 cm wider than the bun (they shrink on cooking). Press a small indentation in the centre with your thumb to prevent them from doming. Season both sides generously with salt and pepper just before cooking.

Heat a cast-iron pan or griddle over very high heat until smoking. Cook the patties for 3 to 4 minutes without moving until a deep dark crust has formed on the underside. Flip once and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more. For medium burgers, the centre should be slightly pink.
Place a slice of cheese on each patty. Add a splash of water to the pan (or cover with a lid) and cook for 30 seconds until the cheese is melted. Rest for 2 minutes.

Toast the buns cut-side down in the same pan for 1 minute. Spread the base with mayonnaise, add lettuce, tomato, and pickles. Place the patty on top. Add ketchup and mustard on the bun lid. Press together and serve immediately.

items.cause: Beef was too lean, or the patty was packed too tightly or overworked
items.fix: Use 20% fat beef mince. Handle the meat as little as possible: just enough to hold the shape. Tight packing causes compaction and toughness.

items.symptom: Patty domes up and does not cook evenly
items.cause: No indentation pressed in the centre before cooking
items.fix: Press a shallow indentation with your thumb in the centre of each patty. The meat expands during cooking and the indentation prevents a dome forming.

content.text: Double cheeseburger: use two 80 g patties per burger instead of one 150 g patty. Bacon cheeseburger: add 2 rashers of streaky bacon cooked until crisp to each burger. BBQ burger: swap the ketchup for BBQ sauce and add grilled onions.
